Title: Flip Normal
Content: Objective Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. Location Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Pattern Flip Normal Operation Select Select/Move tool. Select a Pattern to flip. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Pattern Flip Normal The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. Note: Fold Angle value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).

Title: Zipper Slider Gizmo
Content: List of Contents Zipper Slider Gizmo Move Zipper Slider Rotate Zipper Slide Zipper Slider Gizmo - Rotate or move slider to adjust its distance from zipper tape using its Gizmo. - Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar and select the slider. Move Zipper Slider - While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be moved to access the Gizmo. - Click and drag the blue segment of the Gizmo to move the slider back and forth. - Sliders cannot be moved vertically and horizontally. Rotate Zipper Slide - While the Simulation is deactivated, click the Zipper slider to be rotated to access the Gizmo. - Click and drag the yellow-green circle of the Gizmo to rotate on X axis. - Click and drag the blue circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Y axis. - Click and drag the red circle of the Gizmo to rotate on Z axis. - To rotate the puller only, click the puller again while the slider is selected. - The puller is highlighted in yellow and the Gizmo changes. - To reset the sliders position and angle, right click on the slider and select Reset Slider Arrangement.

Title: Seamline Topstitch
Content: Seamline Topstitch - Establish the Topstitch along the Seamlines. - Select the Seamline Topstitch tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material Seamline Topstitch. - With the Seamline Topstitch tool activated, all the Seamlines appear in the 2D Window. - Hover over the desired Seamline. - A blue guide point should appear and click and drag along the Seamline. - Click again to complete the Seamline Topstitch. - The Seamline Topstitch created on the Seamlines should be highlighted in red. - The Seamline Topstitch tool creates the Topstitch along both sides of the paired Seamlines. Therefore, the blue guide point will appear on both sides of the paired Seamlines. - The Seamline Topstitch tool has some similar qualities with the Free Topstitch tool. Users do not have to select the entire segment of the Seamline. Divide up the Seamlines to apply multiple styles of the Seamline Topstitch on the selected pair of the Seamlines.

Title: Buttonhole
Content: List of Contents Buttonhole Creating a Buttonhole Buttonhole - Create Buttonholes on 3D garment. - Select the Buttonhole tool from the 3D toolbar. Creating a Buttonhole Create a Buttonhole Manually - Select the Buttonhole tool from the 3D toolbar. - Navigate to either the 3D Window or the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as a red dot appears to guide the location. - Click on the desired location to create a Buttonhole. Create a Buttonhole with Designated Values - Select the Buttonhole tool from the 3D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Buttonhole will be created as smart guidelines appear. - Right-click on the desired location to access a pop-up window. The Moving Distance Window will appear. - Enter the desired value in Distance Moved to move the Buttonhole towards right. - Enter the desired value in Position to specifically locate the Buttonhole. - Select OK to complete creating a Buttonhole.

Title: Button
Content: List of Contents Button Creating a Button Button - Create Buttons on 3D garment. - Select the Button tool from the 3D toolbar. Creating a Button Create a Button Manually - Select the Button tool from the 3D toolbar. - Navigate to either the 3D Window or the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Button will be created as a red dot appears to guide the location. - Click on the desired location to create a Button. Create a Button with Designated Values - Select the Button tool from the 3D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D Window and hover the mouse over where the Button will be created as smart guidelines appear. - Right-click on the desired location to access a pop-up window. The Moving Distance Window will appear. - Enter the desired value in Distance Moved to move the Button towards right. - Enter the desired value in Position to specifically locate the Button. - Select OK to complete creating a Button.

Title: Is training available?
Content: CLO for Individual users provides various online training resources on the CLO web as well as social media. 1. CLO Academy Online: Designed &amp created by the CLO 3D Design Team. Intro to CLO- Basic Apparel Design and Intro to CLO- Basic Handbag Design are currently available, with more offerings coming soon. These 2 paid courses go over all the techniques and concepts for creating garments and handbags in CLO. Throughout these courses, there are short quizzes that test your retention of the material. Learners will receive a certification of completion after each course once they are completed. These courses are only available in English at this time. 2. Beginner's Guide to CLO on YouTube: With this free 4-part web tutorial, our expert designers will equip you with all the skills you need to get started using CLO. This training tutorial is made with CLO version 5.0. 3. Youtube tutorial with sound guide available CLO features: This playlist includes all the tools in the CLO 3D window, and how to use them CLO tips and tricks: This playlist includes tutorial videos for intermediate to advanced CLO users looking to learn tips for creating and expressing various garments in CLO *You can also search for tutorial videos in various languages on the CLO Youtube channel. 4. Additional Online training resources Manual -- Find step-by-step instructions for CLO features. Community -- Gain insights and share your expertise with CLO users. Youtube Channel -- Find more video-based tutorials from beginning to advance. 5. Webinar and Workshop You can find bespoke training events by area and language here. 6. CONNECT - Digital sourcing platform for CLO users If you'd rather prefer bespoke training, I advise you to reach out to users in CONNECT as I know some of them offer online training. *CLO offers customized training for Enterprise clients. Please reach out to your CLO Business representative for further information, scheduling, and pricing. Please check our Learning page for more information.

Title: Create Seam Allowance
Content: Objective Create seam allowances on Patterns. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Seam Allowance 2D Toolbar Seam Allowance Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Create Seam Allowance 2D Toolbar Seam Allowance Click on the Pattern outline where seam allowance should be added. Seam allowance is added and colored in grey. Note: Direct editing is not allowed for seam allowances. To edit them, please edit Pattern outlines,

Title: Edit Garment Measure
Content: List of Contents Edit Garment Measure Delete a Garment Measure Edit Garment Measure - Select and delete the measurements created with the Linear Garment Measure tool. - Select the Edit Garment Measure tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to Main Menu and select 3D Garment Measurement Edit Garment Measure. Delete a Garment Measure - Hover the mouse over the measurement created on the 3D garment. When the measurement is highlighted in light blue, right click on the measurement. - Select the DELETE option from the pop-up menu. - Or, select the measurement with the Edit Garment Measure tool and hit the Delete key on the keyboard.

Title: Convert to Segment Point
Content: Convert to Segment Point - Convert a curve point to a segment point - Select the Edit Curve Point tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a curve point and select Convert to Segment Point from the pop-up menu. - The selected curve point will be converted to a segment point.

Title: Show 2D Puckerings
Content: Show 2D Puckering - Show Puckerings in the 2D window even when Puckering tools are not in use. - Select the Show 2D Puckerings tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to and select Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Puckerings - When the Show 2D Puckerings is activated, all Puckering lines will show and disappear from the 2D window.

Title: Segment Puckering
Content: List of Contents Segment Puckering Create Puckering Segment Puckering - Create Puckering to segments of Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. - Select the Segment Puckering tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select Material Puckering Segment Puckering. Create Puckering - Select the Segment Puckering tool from the 2D toolbar. - Hover over the segment to apply Segment Puckering. - The segment will be highlighted. - Click the segment. - The Puckering will be applied to the selected segment.

Title: Change Length
Content: Change Length - Change the length of a segment towards the start, end, or both directions. - Select the Edit Pattern tool. Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment to be edited and select Change Length. The Change Length window will appear. - Select and modify below settings as needed. Start - Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length Window. - For Location, select Start. Then, type in the desired value to Length. - The start point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. End - Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. - For Location, select End. Then, type in the desired value to Length. - The end point of the selected segment will be adjusted based on the designated length value. Both - Follow the instruction above to open the Change Length window. - For Location, select Both. Then, type in the desired value to Length. - Both start and end points of the selected segment will be equally adjusted based on the designated length value.

Title: Create 3D Garment Measure
Content: List of Contents Linear Garment Measure Circumference Garment Measure Objective Measure 3D Garment height and circumference. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Linear/Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Linear Garment Measure / Circumference Garment Measure Operation Linear Garment Measure Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Linear Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Linear Garment Measure Click the beginning point of the Linear Garment Measure on a 3D Garment once. A green dot and rectangle appears. While pressing Shift on keyboard, click the endpoint of the measurement. A vertical measurement with its length is now being created and displayed. Circumference Garment Measure Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Measurement Circumference Garment Measure 3D Toolbar Circumference Garment Measure Click on an area to measure its circumference. A circumference measurement with its value is now being created and displayed.

(Currently only available on Windows PC) Operation C2V file is a file sent from the users to CLO Support Team and V2C is the other way around. This method enables the users to update their account info / product type / the number of license without changing HASP dongle key. Preparations HASP dongle key Upadate_License.exe file C2V file V2C file 1. Creating a C2V file Plug the HASP Key (dongle) into your computer. Title: Match Up
Content: List of Contents Match Up with Pattern Outlines Match Measurement Objective Match up two patterns aligning pattern outlines or points. Or edit the length of both segments to match one side. (ver 7.3) Location 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern (Z) tool Operation Match up with Pattern Outlines Click the tool/menu indicated. After selecting two segments to match each other, Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) Match Up To Start/ To Center/ To End The Patterns align to the Pattern outline that is right clicked on. Match Measurement (ver 7.3) Click the tool/menu indicated. After selecting two segments to match the length, Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Point) Match Up Match Measurement. Set the options as needed and then click the OK button. Match to Choose the reference of the two segments. Direction Select the direction in which the segment will be edited. Measurement The length of the segment to be matched is displayed. The two segments are matched according to the setting options.

Title: The patterns are deformed when I import my DXF file into CLO. How can I fix the problem?
Content: The problem may occur when creating a pattern from 2D CAD software. Please firstly check two things below: If a sewing line or a cutting line of a pattern is made as 'Baseline' from 2D CAD program: If a pattern is created with 'Baselines' from 2D CAD program, the pattern might not be compatible with CLO. For patterns to be imported into CLO, it is recommended to create it with 'Outlines' instead of 'Baselines'. If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program: If a pattern is created as an unclosed shape from 2D CAD program, it might not be compatible with CLO. The feature named 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line' is for importing a pattern into CLO by swapping sewing lines and cutting lines. However, as for patterns created as an unclosed shape, some of the patterns may be deformed when imported into CLO with 'Swap Cutting line and Sewing line'. Thus, please firstly make sure whether a pattern is created as an unclosed shape or not. And if the former, modify the pattern to a closed shape and try to import it into CLO again.

Title: Select/Move Graphic
Content: List of Contents Select Move Objective Select and move graphic. Location Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic 2D/ 3D Toolbar Transform Graphic Operation Select Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic 2D/ 3D Toolbar Transform Graphic Click a graphic. The graphic is selected. When graphics are overlapped, a pop-up window appears allowing users to select the desired graphic (ver.5.1.0). Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select other graphics. Multiple graphics are selected. Or, click and drag in the 2D window. All graphics in the marquee box are selected. Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Graphics Transform Graphic 2D/ 3D Toolbar Transform Graphic Click and drag or use the arrow keys to move graphics. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while dragging the graphics (ver5.0.0.) The graphics move vertically, horizontally, or diagonally at 45. Or, right click or hit the F1(Mac: Ctrl) key to input Distance Moved. Note: Sizing graphic up/down/left/right using Gizmo is only available in 2D Window When graphic over the seamline, it is transformed keeping the original setting. (ver 6.0)

Title: 3D Sewing
Content: List of Contents 3D Sewing Segment Sewing Free Sewing M:N Segment Sewing M:N Free Sewing 3D Sewing - Establish Sewing Lines in the 3D window as the same as in the 2D window. - 3D Toolbar Segment Sewing or Free Sewing Segment Sewing - Click the Segment Sewing tool from the 3D toolbar. - All segments and points of the 3D Garment are highlighted. - Click the first segment to be sewn. - Click the second segment, the pair for the first one. - The Sewing Lines are created in both 2D and 3D windows. Free Sewing - Click theFree Sewing tool from the 3D toolbar. - All segments and points of the 3D Garments are highlighted. - Click to start establishing the first half of the pair. - Drag the mouse as needed and double click to finish the first half. - Click to start establishing the second half of the pair. - Drag the mouse as needed and double click to finish the second half. - The Sewing Lines are created in both 2D and 3D windows. M:N Segment Sewing - Click the M:N Segment Sewing tool from the 3D toolbar. - All segments and points of the 3D Garments are highlighted. - Select all segments to be M Sewing Lines. - Click Enter on the keyboard to complete selecting M. - Select all segments to be N Sewing Lines. - Click Enter on the keyboard to complete selecting N. - M:N Sewing Lines are completed. M:N Free Sewing - Click the M:N Free Sewing tool from the 3D toolbar. - All segments and points of the 3D Garments are highlighted. - Click, drag, and double click to select all segments to be M Sewing Lines. - Click Enter on the keyboard to complete selecting M. - Click, drag, and double click to select all segments to be N Sewing Lines. - Click Enter on the keyboard to complete selecting N. - M:N Sewing Lines are completed.

Title: CLO Fabric Guide
Content: Download our CLO Fabric Guide with detailed explanation about physical properties and textures.

Title: Graphic Grading
Content: Graphic Grading - Apply grading rules to graphics added to Patterns. - Load graphics to Patterns. - Create a Grading Size. - Select the Grading tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select the graphic which grading rule is to be added and navigate to the Property Editor. - Use the arrow keys on the keyboard or desired options to edit Distance or Offset. - Grading rules applied to the graphic only changes its placement, but not size.

Title: Surface Tape Measurement
Content: List of Contents Surface Tape Measurement Measure Length Surface Tape Measurement - Measure specific length of the Avatar, arm length and back length, by going over the curves of the Avatars surface. - Select the Surface Tape Measurement tool from the 3D Toolbar by holding down the Basic Tape Measurement tool for more than two seconds or navigate to and select Main Menu Avatar Measurement Surface Tape Measurement. Measure Length - Select the Surface Tape Measurement tool from the 3D Toolbar by holding down the Basic Tape Measurement tool for more than two seconds. - Click on the Avatar to create the start point. - Drag the mouse as an orange line and point follow along the mouse. - Double click on the Avatar to complete the length measurement. - When the length is measured properly, the line will be highlighted in yellow and the measurement will appear next to the line.

Title: Unfold
Content: Unfold - Draft a half pattern and use Unfold to mirror paste as a single pattern. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern outline which the Pattern will unfold on the basis of. Then, select Unfold from the pop-up menu. - The Pattern will unfold based on the selected Pattern outline.

Title: Internal Polygon/Line
Content: List of Contents Internal Polygon Create Internal Shape Create Internal Shapes with Curves Create Internal Lines with Specific Values Create Internal Lines Create Points in Guidelines Cancel the Last Action Cancel All Actions Internal Polygon - Create Internal Lines and Internal Shapes within Patterns. - Select the Internal Polygon/Line tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D pattern Create Internal Polygon/Line. Create Internal Shape - Select the Internal Polygon/Line tool and click within the Pattern to draw desired shape of Internal Shape. - Click the start point again to complete the Internal Shape. Create Internal Shapes with Curves - Hold down the Ctrl key while clicking within the Pattern to create curves with the free curve point. - Or, click and drag the mouse while adding a point within the Pattern to create curves with AI Bezier handles. Create Internal Lines with Specific Values - Click and then right click within the Pattern to access the Create Internal Polygon window. - Type in the desired values to Length and Position. Create Internal Lines - Click to create a start point. - Continue to click to make the desired shape of an Internal Line. - Double click to complete. Create Points in Guidelines - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to add points in a straight line or a diagonal line. Cancel the Last Action - While creating the Internal Lines or Shapes, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action. Cancel All Actions - While creating the Internal Lines or Shapes, hit the Esc or Ctrl+Z keys on the keyboard to cancel all actions.

Title: Attach Pin to/Detach Pin from Avatar
Content: List of Contents Attach Pin to Avatar Detach Pin from Avatar Objective Affix specific parts of the Garments to the Avatar. This function is commonly used for Simulation or recording animation for avoiding the Garment sliding off from the Avatar. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) Operation Attach Pin to Avatar Create pin to attach on an Avatar. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) Right-click on the created pin select Attach Pin to Avatar/Attach All Pins to Avatar. The selected pin is now being attached to the nearest part of the Avatar. Note: Pins attached to the Avatar is unable to be selected or moved. Detach Pin from Avatar Right-click on the pin attached to the avatar select Detach from Avatar/Detach All Pins from Avatar. The attached pin is now being detached from the Avatar.

Title: Mirror Paste
Content: Objective Mirror Paste copied Pattern/Internal Shape. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) Operation Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Transform Pattern Tool or Edit Pattern Tool. Then, copy the desired Pattern or Internal Shape. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Shape) Mirror Paste (Ctrl + R) The clone of copied Pattern/Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. Click on the 2D window or on the Pattern to place the Pattern or the Internal Shape. Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to move the duplicated Pattern on a straight line or on a diagonal line. Select the desired Pattern and hit Ctrl + C (Copy) / Ctrl +V(Paste), Ctrl + R(Mirror Paste) on the keyboard to copy and paste Patterns to a separate CLO window (ver3.0.0).

Title: HASP Error Message
Content: List of Contents Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) Feature not found (H0031) Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) Too many concurrent useres (H0038) Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) Cause of Error The Server and Client PCs are unable to communicate with each other. Solution Type 'services.msc' in the Run window. In the Service window that follows, check whether or not the status of the Sentinel LDK License Manager is Running. If the status is not Running, right click and select Start. If the status is Started, right click and select Restart. Reboot. If this does not solve the problem, check both versions of the Server and Client PCs HASP Drivers. Make sure both versions are the same. You are able to check the version under Diagnostics. If this does not work, ask your Network Administrator to confirm the Port communication status between the Server and Client. Check whether the 1947 Port is being used by another program. Feature not found (H0031) Cause of Error Despite the dongle key has been recognized, the Feature ID of the program and the Feature ID of the dongle key are different. (This occurs when the wrong version of CLO 3D is installed - i.e. installed the Stand-Alone version for a Network dongle key, and vice versa) Solution Make sure the correct version of CLO 3D is installed. ex&gt Purchased the Network version, but used the Stand-Alone version's installer. -&gt Re-install CLO 3D using the Network version's installer. Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) Objective Cause of Error - When the HASP Key is not plugged in to the PC. - Network Version only: the Client PC does not recognize the Server PC that the dongle key is connected to. - When the HASP Key is recognized, but the Sentinel License Manager service fails to start properly. Solution Make sure the HASP is connected to the PC. Check the red light of the HASP Key. It should light up when plugged in to the PC. Check whether or not the HASP Key shows up in the ACC page (refer to the image below). If the red light, or the ACC page does not look equal to the image above, refer to the following manual, reinstall the Sentinel HASP Driver. Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation Too many concurrent users (H0038) Cause of Error When the number of users connected to the program exceeds the maximum allowed number of users. ex&gt If the maximum number of users (the number of purchased licenses) is 2, and 3 users try to log-in, the last person to attempt a connection will receive an error message. Solution Check the number of current users via the link below. Connect when one of the current users exit the program. ACC Page Click Sentinel Keys, on the left. When the Key shows up as the image above, click Sessions, on the right. The following page should display the current user(s). Connect when one of the current users exits the program. If any unauthorized user is connected, click the Disconnect button on the right to log the person out of the program. Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) Cause of Error The HASP Driver has not been properly installed on the PC, or the Driver is damaged. To confirm whether it being properly installed, enter http://localhost:1947 or http://127.0.0.1:1947 into your web browser, or click on the following link ( ACC Page ). If the following page does not look equal to the image below, there is a problem with the Sentinel HASP Driver. Solution Refer to the following manual and reinstall the HASP Driver. HASP Driver Installation Go Back to the List of Contents

Title: [Popup] Show/Hide Topstitch
Content: Objective Show or hide Topstitches as needed. Location Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Topstitches 2D Toolbar Show 2D Topstitches Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Materials Show 2D Topstitches 2D Toolbar Show 2D Topstitches All Topstitches in the 2D window is now going to be displayed or hidden.

Title: Fold Pattern
Content: Objective Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. Location Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Operation Click on an Internal Line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Adjust the value of Fold Angle as desired. Note: Fold Strength Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. Fold Angle Sets the value in the range of 0 to 360, 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Rendering Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.)

Title: Open/Save Tape Measure
Content: Objective Save a created tape measure in .mea file format. Open a saved tape measure to reuse it. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open /Save Operation Open Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open Open File window appears. Select a desired file and click Open. Save Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Save Save File window appears. Select a desired location to store. Enter a desired file name and click Save. .mea file is now being created.

Title: How can I join CLO Discord?
Content: Account Creation Go to https://discord.com/ Create an account Choose how you want to access Discord Option 1: Choose to download the Discord app for your desktop Option 2: Choose to access Discord in your browser Joining the CLO Discord Server Copy the CLO Discord server invitation link to your Clipboard https://bit.ly/CLOOFFICIAL Open the Discord Desktop App Click on the Add a Server Button on the left side of the interface In the Create a Server Pop-up, Click Join a Server at the bottom Paste the server link in the Invite Link field, then click Join Server The CLO icon will now appear on the left side of your interface. Go to the Notice channels on the left side. Please read the Rules and Read me First text channels Go to the Self-Roles channel and react with the blue dot to gain full access to all of the CLO channels You will now see all of the different CLO text channels. Happy CLOing!
